newsitem.title: UKRAINE: IMF mission leaves Ukraine, no decision yet on EFF.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission leaves Ukraine, no decision yet on EFF.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission has ended talks in Ukraine promising to pay the last tranche of a stand-by loan but with no decision on a new multi-billion-dollar credit, a presidential aide said on Friday.

"Our talks have ended very well. We have the IMF's word that a positive decision on the ninth tranche, worth $90 million, of the stand-by will be taken next week," President Leonid Kuchma's economic aide Valery Litvitsky said by telephone.
"As far as the EFF (Extended Fund Facility) is concerned, Ukraine must pass a budget on a new tax basis. The IMF will decide on the EFF after the budget is passed," he added.
The mission, which arrived on January 29 and was due to leave on Friday, came for talks on the $2.5-3.0 billion EFF which is to follow the $860 million stand-by loan.
They also held "Article Four" consultations undertaken every year with credit recipients. No comment was available from the IMF on results of the talks.
Ukraine's parliament is expected to give the 1997 budget a second reading in March but the IMF wants tax reforms to be passed before then.
"The main problem is the budget. There are no other key problems. We will reach an agreement with the IMF," Litvinsky said.

Kuchma has said the budget will be passed by the end of the first quarter, and a spokeswoman for Deputy Prime Minister Viktor Pynzenyk said the new credit could be agreed and the first money paid out a month after that.
